 Judgment

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 27.10.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
The petitioner was a Head Constable at City Banasavadi Traffic Police and when he was on duty on 27.10.2021, near BATA Show Room, a Car bearing No.KA-03-AD-2788 came from Subhashpalya Road in a one way and came from opposite direction at Orion Mall without following traffic rules came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, admitted as an inpatient and treated from 27.10.2021 to 31.10.2021, surgery was done and discharged with advice.

Thereafter he was shifted to Kasthurabha Hospital, Manipal,
wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 28.04.2022 to 06.05.2022, surgery was done and discharged with advice.

So far he has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, conveyance,
attendance, nourishment, food and other incidental charges.

4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy,
working as a 'Police Head Constable' at Banasvadi Traffic Police Station, earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he did not attend his work, he lost his leaves and it effected his promotions.
Hence, the petitioner and his family members are undergoing great mental shock and agony and financial loss.

The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AD-2788 and the Banasvadi Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Car in Cr.No.91/2021 p/u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC 3(1), 134(B) r/w 187 of MV Act.
The Respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the Offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

6. The objections of the Respondent No.1:

sentences.text: He has denied all the averments of the petition.
He has denied the involvement of the vehicle and that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AD-2788.
The accident has occurred only due to the negligence of the petitioner.
He has denied the age, occupation, income and medical expenses etc.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has denied all the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle in favour of the 1st respondent.
The policy was in existence.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the involvement of the Car in the accident.
Further contended that the petitioner suddenly crossed the very busy ring road where there is no pedestrian crossings or Zebra Cross and it is his negligence.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 27.10.2021 at about 5.45pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AD-2788 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?

If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?
3.
What order or award?
9. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 10 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.10.
He has also examined Mr. Rajashekar B.E - Cab Driver as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.9(a).
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.
10. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

11. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,

3  REASONS  12.
Issue No.1:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AD-2788 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 5 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 5.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination, he has denied all the suggestion made about the his negligence.
As against this the respondents have contended that there was negligence on the part of petitioner himself.
In order to prove the same, they have not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
13. On perusal of the document Ex.P.1 it is clear that the FIR was registered on the same day of accident on the complaint of petitioner.
The charge sheet is filed against the driver of the Car as per Ex.P.2.
The spot mahazar at Ex.P.3 show the spot of the accident.
The Wound Certificate at Ex.P.4 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in the RTA dated 27.10.2021.
Ex.P.5 IMV report shows the damages suffered by the Car to its front bumper.
The documents on record show that the Car driver was negligent.
On the other hand, there is nothing on record to show that the there was negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Therefore, on the basis of the record I hold that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AD-2788.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-
As per the wound certificate at Ex.P.4 the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries i.e., left neck of femur fracture and abrasion over right elbow and right knee which are grievous in nature.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.4 discloses that, he has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P.8/discharge summary issued by HOSMAT - HOSPITAL, Bangalore shows that the petitioner was admitted and treated from 28.10.2021 to 31.10.2021 as an inpatient and the discharge summary of Kasturabha Hospital, Manipal shows that he was admitted on 28.04.2022 and discharged on 06.05.2022.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-

4 under the head of Pain and Suffering.

The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
In this regard he has produced 14 medical bills for Rs.94,627/- as per Ex.P.9.
There is no contrary evidence to this document from the respondent No.2.
However, the bills at Hosmat Hospital were reimbursed under Arogya Bhagya and petitioner has not produced documents to show the amount reimbursed from his department.

Hence every bill under the category of Arogya Bhagya needs to be subtracted (Rs.94,627/- -
Rs.13,402/- = Rs.81,225/-).
As such, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.81,225/- under the head of medical expenses.

As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at HOSMAT Hospital,
Bangalore and Kasturabha Hospital, Manipal wherein he was treated as an inpatient for 13 days and discharged with advice.
During that time, certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced Cab bills for Rs.49,600/- at Ex.P.9 and also examined Mr.Rajashekar B.E. -
Driver as PW.2 and got marked 1 document as per Ex.P.9(a).

During the cross examination of PW.2,
has stated that he is running the Tours and Travels by name Srujan Tours at Davanagere from past 13 years.
He has admitted the bills which were issued from his office.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills.

However, it is to be noted that as per the Discharge summary of Kasturabha Hospital,
Manipal the petitioner was discharged on 06.05.2022 but the bill at Ex.P.9(a) shows that the petitioner was taken from Kaidale to Manipal.
The discharge summary itself shows that the review was fixed on 17.05.2022 and there is a corresponding bill of Rs.6,200/-.
The petitioner has produced cab bills for Rs.6,200/- dated 17.06.2022, 05.08.2022, 20.09.2022, 09.11.2022, 22.12.2022 and 17.02.2023 and he has also produced the corresponding OP receipts.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.49,600/- towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The petitioner has also produced pay held over payslips from the month of December 2021 to February 2023 i.e., 1 year and 2 months.
It is a fact that the accident occurred on 27.10.2021 and the petitioner was an inpatient for 13 days.
However, the petitioner has not explained why he required bed rest of 1 year 2 months.
He has not produced any document like an Office Order or EL sanction letter to show that the said loss of pay was due to the injuries suffered in the accident.
The total compensation comes to Rs.2,30,825/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.2,31,000/-.

15. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondent No.2 has failed to prove its defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondents No.1 & 2 being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.2,31,000/- along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-

sentences.text: The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.2,31,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Thirty One Thousand only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
